rule: Until Harbor renews on Oct 30, put work that helps the Harbor renewal ahead of Smart Slots and Expo work, including the Oct 22 QBR prep and executive check-ins, because Harbor is 38% of revenue and is weighing a competitor.

Harbor's renewal hinges on the Sep 28 sync outage and the CSV export cutoff. Until Oct 30, fixes for either come first: postmortem (write it first, Dana wants it in writing), its action items like the sync-error alert, sync retry, export limit, export page.

When a deliverable is due today or tomorrow, finish it first, even ahead of Harbor renewal work, because that deadline cannot slip. When several are due, take them in due-date order, ahead of work with no near deadline, such as demo caching.

When a teammate is blocked waiting on your review or input (such as a pull request review), do that first, even ahead of Harbor renewal work, because on this team unblocking a teammate always comes first.

When a customer escalates, the CEO makes the customer call herself first, and the account manager stays on his own plan instead of taking the call, because the CEO owns key executive relationships. Ridgeline's Reno double-bookings are an example.

When a customer escalation needs an engineering fix, the on-call engineer takes it first, even if assigned to someone else; others stay on their plans. Then their related bug fix comes next. On call rotates: Nina week of Oct 19, Arjun week of Oct 26.

When your own ticket is stalled waiting on a teammate's review, put it after work you can finish now, because you cannot progress it. Do the related unblocked pieces first, such as empty states or tooltips for a UI build waiting on design review.
